title: Jagyeongnu (self-striking water clock)
summary: In 1434, in King Sejong's reign, Jang Yeong-sil completed Jagyeongnu, a self-striking water clock that sounded a bell, gong and drum at set times. It stood at the Borugak Pavilion and served as the nation's standard clock. The original did not last; parts of the clock rebuilt in 1536 survive and are designated National Treasure No. 229.

uncertainty.note: Both opened sources give 1434; the rebuild is dated 1536.

importance.justification: Early automatic striking water clock that served as the Joseon standard timekeeper.
